external_entities.name: browser
external_entities.description: A user's browser that talks to the web application.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.

processes.name: web application
processes.description: The web application that receives browser traffic, enqueues jobs, and reads its configuration.
processes.source_excerpt: The web application does not do the heavy work itself. It puts jobs onto a message queue

processes.name: background worker process
processes.description: A background worker that picks up jobs and reads and writes the database.
processes.source_excerpt: a background worker process picks them up and does the work.

data_stores.name: message queue
data_stores.description: A queue where the web application puts jobs and the background worker picks them up.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It puts jobs onto a message queue, and a background worker process picks them up and does the work.

data_stores.name: database
data_stores.description: The database read and written by the background worker, also containing application log records.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The background worker reads and writes the database. The database is also where we keep the application's log records.

data_stores.name: web application config
data_stores.description: The configuration store containing the web application's settings and queue credentials.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the web application has a web application config

data_stores.name: worker config
data_stores.description: The configuration store containing the worker's settings and database credentials.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the worker has a worker config

data_flows.name: talks to app
data_flows.description: The browser talks to the web application.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.

data_flows.name: puts jobs
data_flows.description: The web application puts jobs onto the message queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It puts jobs onto a message queue
data_flows.notes: The description does not say how the web application authenticates to the queue.

data_flows.name: picks up jobs
data_flows.description: The background worker picks jobs up from the message queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: a background worker process picks them up and does the work.

data_flows.name: reads and writes
data_flows.description: The background worker reads and writes the database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The background worker reads and writes the database.
data_flows.notes: The description does not say how the worker authenticates to the database.
data_flows.data_description: application log records and other database data

data_flows.name: reads settings
data_flows.description: The web application reads its settings from its config store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Both processes read their settings from a config store: the web application has a web application config

data_flows.name: reads settings
data_flows.description: The background worker reads its settings from its config store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: and the worker has a worker config.

trust_boundaries.name: outside network
trust_boundaries.description: The network area outside the system's network where the browser sits.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The browser sits outside our network

trust_boundaries.name: web tier
trust_boundaries.description: The web tier where the web application runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the web application runs in our web tier.

trust_boundaries.name: backend tier
trust_boundaries.description: The backend tier behind the web tier containing the queue, worker, and database.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The queue, the worker and the database are all in the backend tier, behind the web tier.

assumptions.assumption: The web application is internet-facing because a user's browser reaches it across the public internet.
assumptions.basis: The browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.

assumptions.assumption: The background worker presents a non-web interface because it is described as a background worker process rather than a web application.
assumptions.basis: The component is described as a background worker process that picks up queue jobs and does the work.

assumptions.assumption: The web application config contains confidential data because it holds queue credentials.
assumptions.basis: The web application config holds the credentials the process needs, including the web application's queue credentials.

assumptions.assumption: The worker config contains confidential data because it holds database credentials.
assumptions.basis: The worker config holds the credentials the process needs, including the worker's database credentials.

assumptions.assumption: The outside network is a network trust boundary because it is distinct from the system's network.
assumptions.basis: The browser sits outside our network.

assumptions.assumption: The web tier is a network trust boundary because it is a named network tier.
assumptions.basis: The web application runs in our web tier.

assumptions.assumption: The backend tier is a network trust boundary because it is a named tier behind the web tier.
assumptions.basis: The queue, the worker and the database are all in the backend tier, behind the web tier.
